title: A Fish Swarm 7 Kilometres Long Gets Hunted by Dolphins and Sharks

scenes.text: A school of fish seven kilometres long is hunted every winter.
In South Africa's sardine run, shoals stretch over seven kilometres long, one and a half wide, and thirty metres deep.
Up to 18,000 dolphins herd them into tight balls. Sharks and seals move in. Thousands of gannets dive from the sky.
Even Bryde's whales lunge straight through the middle.
A bait ball rarely lasts longer than ten minutes.
Seven kilometres of fish, and every predator showed up.

description:
Every winter, sardines stream along South Africa's east coast in shoals that can be over 7 km long, 1.5 km wide and 30 m deep.
Up to 18,000 dolphins, plus sharks, seals, gannets and Bryde's whales, gather to feed. A single bait ball rarely lasts longer than ten minutes.
Would you dive into a sardine run to film it?

first_comment: The run happens between roughly May and July when the water drops below about 21 degrees C. Which predator would you most want to see up close?
